instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Call It a Fair Win
cards.instruction: Get them to recognize the result as deserved rather than accidental, gifted, or manipulated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: In the quiz-club newsletter, say I earned the trophy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There were a lot of bird questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that in. I studied birds for six months and got all twelve right.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You were lucky they asked them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Call the questions lucky and my answers earned.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You saw the finish. Say I won that race fairly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They slowed near the end.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can mention them slowing. Just don't say they handed me the race.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One of them stopped to tie a shoe.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them I checked my knots. I'll settle for winning on preparation.

cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Take the Consequence
cards.instruction: Get them to accept responsibility for carrying out the cost, penalty, or unpleasant next step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You lost the chess game. The agreement says you wash up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought we were joking.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You weren't joking while you were winning. I'll dry; you wash.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't we play again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the dishes. I'll set the board up while you finish the pans.

cards.title: Show Me the Score
cards.instruction: Find out how they measure success, what they stand to gain, and where you currently rank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When you call my picnic a success, what are you measuring?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Everyone having fun.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll collect the guest comments. Where do I rank against last year's organiser?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Beat their sandwich total and I can ask for a bigger picnic budget.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Show me last year's total. We'll count mine together before you ask for the money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: What do you gain if your cousin beats me in the club election?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A competent president.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me one proposal to price. What would make me as competent?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The car park needs resurfacing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll cost it. If I get you that car park, do I move ahead of your cousin on your ballot?

cards.title: Enter on My Side
cards.instruction: Recruit them into your side of a contest or bargain before the stakes become fully clear.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put on our blue quiz-team badge before I explain the final round.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why? What happens if we lose?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll answer the last question. You only have to wear the badge.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I haven't agreed to face anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Start with a blue ribbon, then. You choose where to tie it.

cards.title: Raise the Stakes
cards.instruction: Persuade them to accept a larger risk, cost, or commitment so the outcome will feel decisive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's make this chess game decide who cooks all weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were playing for a biscuit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the biscuit. I'll do the washing-up if you lose; you still cook.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want you ordering three-course meals.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You choose the menu. But whoever loses feeds us until Monday. Agreed?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you put your club captaincy on the rematch?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a ridiculous risk.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For one week, then. If I lose, I'll clean everyone's kit for that week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Isn't pride enough?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can't even remember who won the last six. Your captaincy against my kit duty, for one week. Shake?
